zh-CN.Map a cabinet filler against an uneven w: Map a cabinet filler against an uneven wall with a worked survey, blank width, station table, downloadable CSV and profile diagram.
zh-CN.A straight cabinet next to an uneven wal: A straight cabinet next to an uneven wall leaves a gap that changes with height. A filler closes that gap while preserving the cabinet position and the clearance needed for doors or handles. This worked example focuses on one face-plane filler after the cabinet is positioned. It supplements the general filler guide with a traceable survey and a numerical blank check. Every dimension here is invented for teaching; the diagram and CSV are not a measured job or a cutting pattern for another room.
zh-CN.Set the cabinet in its intended final lo: Set the cabinet in its intended final location, level and plumb as required by the installation plan. Establish the straight vertical cabinet edge in the finished face plane as x = 0; measure horizontally from that line toward the wall. Measure height y downward from the top of the proposed filler. Mark both references on a sketch and identify the face side. The example assumes the cabinet is already held in its final position throughout surveying and fitting. If the cabinet moves, or the face plane changes, the recorded gaps no longer describe the same geometry and must be surveyed again.
zh-CN.Record the Wall at Named Stations: Record the Wall at Named Stations
zh-CN.At y = 0, 200, 400, 600 and 800 mm, the: At y = 0, 200, 400, 600 and 800 mm, the hypothetical gaps are respectively 42, 45, 49, 46 and 43 mm. The measured range is 42–49 mm, a 7 mm variation; the arithmetic mean of these five readings is 45 mm. A 45 mm blank cannot reach the wall at the 49 mm station even though it equals the sample mean. Equally, five points do not establish the largest gap or the exact shape between them. Check the whole contact line for local bulges, depressions, trim, and obstructions; collect additional stations wherever the surface changes. The drawn connecting lines are only illustrative.
zh-CN.Choose a Blank With a Defined Margin: Choose a Blank With a Defined Margin
zh-CN.Assume a straight 55 mm wide, 800 mm lon: Assume a straight 55 mm wide, 800 mm long blank with its cabinet-side edge on x = 0 and its outer edge at x = 55. Relative to the five measurements, the nominal material outside the wall line is 13, 10, 6, 9 and 12 mm. At the largest observed gap the remaining 6 mm is a provisional working margin, not proof that the whole wall is covered or that a tool can be safely used. Check stock straightness, the full wall profile, the transfer setup and the planned trimming method. Select a wider blank or revisit the installation if the actual maximum or the required setup exceeds that margin.
zh-CN.A full-width blank overlaps the wall in: A full-width blank overlaps the wall in the final face plane, so it cannot simply be put there untrimmed. Temporarily hold a template in front of the cabinet and wall, clear of the obstruction, with its straight edge projected to the same cabinet datum and its top aligned to the survey origin. Transfer the wall contour to the template using a suitable scribing setup, preserving its lateral and vertical reference and orientation. If the marking tool introduces a lateral offset, account for and test that offset before transferring the line to the blank; a side-on wall profile or a change of plane is not automatically the face-plane contour. Scribing transfers the actual adjoining contour; a strip template can be useful when direct access or multiple surfaces make the setup difficult [1, 2]. The station measurements are independent checks on that transferred line, not permission to draw straight chords between sparse readings. Confirm which side of the line is waste and test the setup on inexpensive material if the reference or tool offset is uncertain.
zh-CN.Trim in Stages and Check the Physical Fi: Trim in Stages and Check the Physical Fit
zh-CN.The wall-side waste lies beyond the tran: The wall-side waste lies beyond the transferred contour, toward the 55 mm outer edge in this example. Remove material conservatively with work supported and equipment used according to its instructions; leave the line initially and refine in small steps. Move the trimmed filler into the intended face plane at the same datum and check for contact, gaps and interference along the entire height. Do not force the cabinet out of plumb to make the filler fit. If the line passes outside the blank, a hidden obstruction changes the fit, or the cabinet shifts, stop and remeasure instead of concealing the error with a claimed exact fit.
zh-CN.Fit and Door Clearance Are Separate Chec: Fit and Door Clearance Are Separate Checks
zh-CN.A wall-hugging edge does not establish t: A wall-hugging edge does not establish that the cabinet door, hinge, handle or drawer can operate. Check the actual opening path with the selected hardware and adjacent wall or trim, including the handle projection. The five gap readings describe only distances in one face plane; they do not model a three-dimensional wall, hardware swing or attachment strength. If clearance is insufficient, revise the cabinet position or filler design before final fixing. Verify the chosen attachment method, accessible fasteners and finish requirements for the actual cabinet and wall.
zh-CN.Use the Download as a Survey Record: Use the Download as a Survey Record
zh-CN.The CSV records the five heights and gap: The CSV records the five heights and gaps, the common datum, 55 mm blank and calculated station waste. It is a teaching record, not a direct-import contract or a full-size cutting template. For a real installation replace every example number with measurements from the installed position, add the project and revision, record the plane and measurement method, and retain notes about obstructions. After a test fit, annotate the changes and verify again. The profile diagram deliberately uses different horizontal and vertical scales to make the small variation visible, so it must never be printed as a pattern.
zh-CN.Before final attachment confirm that the: Before final attachment confirm that the cabinet remains in its approved position, the fitted edge follows the full contact line, the visible joint and finish meet the project expectation, and the door and handle clear the wall throughout their movement. Record any changed dimensions and preserve the final survey with the installation notes. A filler sized from the installed cabinet can absorb an irregular boundary, but it does not replace the checks for the cabinet mounting, supports, site conditions or manufacturer hardware requirements.
zh-CN.Fix and identify the cabinet datum and f: Fix and identify the cabinet datum and face plane before taking readings.
zh-CN.Inspect the whole contact line and recor: Inspect the whole contact line and record additional changes between stations.
zh-CN.Check blank coverage and the practical t: Check blank coverage and the practical transfer and trimming margin.
zh-CN.Transfer the actual profile, keep the ca: Transfer the actual profile, keep the cabinet reference and test-fit in stages.
zh-CN.Verify door and handle clearance and the: Verify door and handle clearance and the final attachment before release.
zh-CN.How can a filler blank be checked agains: How can a filler blank be checked against a crooked wall without losing the cabinet datum?
zh-CN.Survey the actual gap from a fixed cabin: Survey the actual gap from a fixed cabinet reference, retain enough blank width for the largest observed gap, then transfer the complete wall profile and verify the fit.
